lawyer:
Md. Ashfaqul Islam, Advocate ----- For the Petitioners. 
Dewan AMS Zaman, Deputy-Attorney-General ----- For the Opposite Party
parties:
Jasimuddin (Md) and another ------ Petitioners
vs.
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
The petitioners obtained this Rule against judgment and order passed by the Assistant Judge, 3rd Court Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 8 of 1991 on 18.5.92, restoring Title Suit No. 19 of 1991. 

 2. The petitioners filed Title Suit Nd. 787 of 1978 against the Government Opposite Party which was decreed ex parte on 6.3.84 declaring title of the petitioners in 0041 acres of land of dagh No. 549 of mouza Meradia, Dhaka. The Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh instituted Title Suit No. 138 of 1990 in the court of Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka, for setting aside the ex parte decree dated 6.3.84 made in title suit No.787 of 1978. The petitioners contested the suit. The suit was subsequently transferred to the court of Assistant Judge, Additional3rd Court Dhaka. The Government appeared in that court and filed hazira and received copy of the written statement on 5.3.91. The suit, however, was dismissed for default on 30.3.91. The Government opposite party thereafter instituted Miscellaneous Case No. 8 of 1991 for setting aside the ex parte decree dismissing the suit and restoration of the suit on the ground that it had no knowledge of transfer of the suit to the court of Additional Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka. 

 3. The petitioner contested the said Miscellaneous case on the assertion that transfer of suit was notified on the doors of the shertaders of the transfer courts regarding the transfer of the present suit and the transfer of the suit was within knowledge of the Government. On 5.3.91, the date fixed for serving copy of the written statement, the Government appeared but the defendants were absent. It also appears from the order of that date that Government took copy of the written statement filed by the petitioner before me. 

 5. Mr. Ashfaqul Islam vehemently submits that the impugned order in the application under Order IX rule 9 for setting aside ex parte decree dismissing the suit of the Government has been made without application of judicial mind inasmuch as from the order dated 5.3.91 on the ground upon which application for setting aside the ex parte decree of dismissing the suit was made palpably shows that the learned Judge did not apply his mind in making the impugned order. Mr. Ashfaq has drawn my attention to order of the transferer court made on 5.3.91. On perusal of the same it appears that the Government filed hazira on that date before the transferer court, the Additional Assistant Judge 3rd Court, Dhaka and also received written statement filed by the defendant. Thus, in view of such position it appears that the Government had knowledge about the transfer of the suit. In view of such facts how the learned Assistant Judge passed the impugned order is not understandable to me. For, this conduct of the Government in proceeding with the suit it was proper on the part of the learned Judge also to take into consideration the ground upon which the case has been filed while making the order sought to be set aside. But in this case statement made in the application by Government through his agent exposes it to criticism by the court of law. The Government and his agent should be careful in making statement against the order of the Court for making out the case for the Government. The ground upon which the government sought to set aside decree of the dismissal of the suit seems to be unfounded. In order to set aside an order made ex parte the party which seeks such order should be clear in making the ground for setting aside the order and the court should not exercise its jurisdiction in allowing such application without application of its mind to the facts of the case. This material aspect unfortunately, was not noticed by the court in making the impugned order and this has caused failure of justice. Accordingly, I set aside the order. In the result, the Rule is made absolute with cost of Taka 500.00 (five hundred) only.
